title: Incremental Output and Adaptive Tooling PRD (Hosted API) - Draft
body:
Summary:

This PRD proposes an iteration of the Hosted API surface that makes incremental (partial) output first-class, introduces an adaptive tool invocation protocol, and defines ergonomic SDK primitives for common developer patterns. The aim is to reduce end-to-end latency for interactive apps, reduce developer friction when wiring model output to external tools, and improve the reliability of structured outputs for downstream processing.

Context & problem statement:
- Customers building chat assistants, code helpers, and real-time experiences want: earliest-possible partial tokens, typed/parseable blocks (tables, JSON objects), and predictable tool handoffs.
- Current Hosted API supports streaming tokens and tool calling, but:
  - streaming is token-focused not semantic-chunk focused (clients must reassemble or guess boundaries),
  - tool calling is a best-effort pattern without standardized lifecycle hooks (start/confirm/abort/retry),
  - SDK ergonomics are inconsistent between languages which leads to client-side duplicated glue code.
- These gaps increase engineering time for customers and raise error rates when tool invocations miss required context or when partial streaming fragments are interpreted prematurely.

Objectives (what success looks like):
- Latency: enable first-meaningful-chunk delivery median < 180ms for 90% of short-turn chat requests in hosted regions.
- Developer productivity: reduce common customer integration glue by providing SDK primitives and canonical patterns; measured by a 30% reduction in reference integration code in starter templates.
- Reliability of tool calls: reduce tool invocation error rate in our staged tests by 50% via lifecycle confirmations and structured frames.
- Observability: provide per-request telemetry (time to first-chunk, time to tool-invoke, tool success/fail) surfaced in Console and logs.

Non-goals:
- Full contract-first schema enforcement at the server side (we provide soft validation + helpful errors, not hard rejection for initial rollouts).
- Replacing customer business logic for tool orchestration.

User personas:
- Frontend engineer building a multi-user chat product (needs token streaming + stable chunk boundaries).
- Backend platform engineer wiring model output to enterprise systems (needs durable tool invocation semantics and retries).
- Library author building SDK wrappers (needs simple, composable primitives).

Scope of work (high level):
1) Incremental chunk API semantics and streaming frames.
2) Adaptive tool invocation lifecycle and typed tool results.
3) Structured semantic frames for parseable output (soft schema binding).
4) SDK ergonomic patterns across JS/Python minimal set first.
5) Telemetry and Console views for new metrics and events.

Detailed proposals:
1) Incremental / chunked streaming model
- Idea: stream "semantic chunks" in addition to raw token deltas. A chunk = minimal coherent unit (sentence, JSON object, table row) that the model signals via a chunk marker.
- Protocol: streaming frames include a header field "frame_type": ["token", "chunk_start", "chunk_data", "chunk_end", "event"]. Clients can opt-in to chunked streaming by setting request param streaming_mode="chunks".
- Benefits: clients can render partial but meaningful content (e.g., a completed JSON object to parse into UI) without waiting for whole response or parsing fragile token boundaries.
- Backpressure and flow control: server sends chunk_start with estimated_length; SDK exposes an async iterator plus a backpressure token allowing clients to request pause/resume for slow UIs.

2) Adaptive Tool Invocation Protocol (ATIP)
- Problem: tool invocations today are a fire-and-forget call embedded in text. We need lifecycle.
- Protocol: tool_call frames with lifecycle: {request -> confirm -> execute -> result -> ack}. Each tool is identified by a stable id and schema.
- The model can emit a tool_call frame that includes context, requested inputs, and a confidence estimate. The client may: auto-execute, prompt the user for approval, or transform inputs then execute.
- Retries and idempotency: tool_call includes a client-visible call_id which the server persists for short window to deduplicate retries.

3) Structured semantic frames & schema binding
- Provide a way for models to annotate structured blocks with an optional schema_id and version. A lightweight validation is run in the hosted pipeline to produce a validation status: {ok|warning|error} and a short error reason.
- For example: a model emits an action block with schema_id="order.line_item.v1". Hosted service validates shape and attaches validation metadata.
- We intentionally do not enforce rejection on first release; instead we return deterministic warnings and recommended fixes to improve model prompts/finetunes.

4) SDK ergonomics: primitives & patterns
- JS & Python initial primitives:
  - streamChunks(request): async iterator yielding either TokenDelta or Chunk objects with metadata.
  - onToolCall(callback): SDK registers handler that receives tool_call frames and resolves with tool result. Handler returns {status: "ok", payload: {...}} or {status: "defer"/"abort"}.
  - structuredFrame.parse(schema): convenience helper that attempts to parse & validate and returns (object | ValidationError).
- High-level patterns:
  - client-side confirm-pattern: an optional prompt UX hook that pauses execution until user confirmation, then resumes the model stream.
  - optimistic-exec: auto-run low-risk tools then patch model with tool result (model receives result via event injection).
- Backwards compatibility: default behavior remains the token-stream behavior unless streaming_mode="chunks" or tool_handlers provided.

5) Observability & telemetry
- New telemetry events per request: first_chunk_received_at, first_meaningful_chunk_at, tool_call_requested_at, tool_call_executed_at, tool_call_result_at, structured_validation_status.
- Console: new per-route timeline visualization and per-request tooling waterfall that shows streaming chunks and tool events, with hoverable payload previews (redacted).
- Logs & export: events available via existing logs export (BigQuery/S3) and included in the trace-level JSON for postmortem.

Backward compatibility & migration
- Default hosted API remains unchanged for legacy clients. New query params and response frame_types are opt-in.
- SDKs will include compatibility layers: legacyStream(request) -> token stream, streamChunks(request) -> chunked stream.

Rollout plan (90-day roadmap high level)
- Week 0–3: internal prototype + spec finalized; model producer task to emit chunk markers; wire frame envelope in runtime.
- Week 4–8: implement server-side framing, basic validation hooks, JS+Python SDK prototypes.
- Week 9–12: beta with 10 customers; Console telemetry UI alpha and logs export.
- Week 13–16: iterate on error modes, add pause/resume backpressure, enlarge beta cohort.
- Week 17–20: GA for streaming chunks (soft enforcement), team-run migration docs and starter templates.

Risks & mitigations
- Risk: model chunk markers inconsistent across model families. Mitigation: provide prompt templates, small fine-tune/PEFT tasks and quality checks; progressively tighten validation.
- Risk: increased complexity for SDK maintainers. Mitigation: keep primitives minimal and shared across languages; provide canonical reference implementations.
- Risk: abuse surface for long-running tool calls. Mitigation: enforce per-request timeouts and tool rate limits at the host layer.

Open questions (action items)
- Should we expose server-side hard schema enforcement for select enterprise routes? (security/compliance tradeoffs)
- How many chunk types do we accept initially? (sentence/json/table/code-block)
- What is the persistence window for call_id deduplication? (default 60s vs configurable)

Appendix: Example minimal chunked stream (conceptual)
- Client request: {
  model: "rwd-llama-4e",
  streaming_mode: "chunks",
  tool_handlers: ["search", "calendar"]
}

- Sample frames (newline-delimited server stream):
  {"frame_type":"chunk_start","chunk_id":"c-1","chunk_kind":"json","schema_id":"task.v1"}
  {"frame_type":"chunk_data","chunk_id":"c-1","data":"{\"task\": \"book flight\"}"}
  {"frame_type":"chunk_end","chunk_id":"c-1"}
  {"frame_type":"event","event_type":"tool_call","tool_call":{"call_id":"call-42","tool_id":"calendar.create","inputs":{"date":"2026-01-12"}}}

Next steps:
- Review with infra (runtime framing & perf implications) and research (model prompt templates + validation heuristics) by 2025-11-10.
- Align JS/py SDK minimal API surface and ship reference code for beta customers.

Notes to reviewers:
- Focus feedback on the developer ergonomics and the proposed chunk frame shapes (would these meet common integration patterns?).
- If you have customer examples of brittle token-boundary parsing, paste them into the Confluence doc linked above.
